intro: These questions are kept out of every exam, custom mix, Mistakes and Starred list because neither the slides nor the TA's pen marks settle the answer. Each one shows the question cropped from the original PDF, so you can work it out yourself, with a link to that week's PDF and a note on what makes it uncertain.

items.label: Q4 (3 Oct)
items.q: Looking at Figure 4 (distance between real and inferred user home city, for INCORRECT inferences only), which dataset shows the largest share of its incorrect inferences falling within 50 km of the true city?
options: All three datasets are statistically indistinguishable
items.mark: The TA ticked A and drew a line at 50 km on the inset.
items.why: In the inset of Fig. 4, the Foursquare curve (solid green) is highest at 50 km, at about 0.46; Google+ and Twitter are both near 0.25. That matches option B, not the printed key A. No curve reaches 0.87 at 50 km.

items.label: Practice test Q51
items.q: What is the difference between Pearson and Spearman rank correlation?
options: Pearson assesses linear relationships; Spearman evaluates monotonic relationships

items.why: A and C are both true and B is false, so "All of the above" is wrong, yet the question expects a single option.

items.label: Q32 (12 Sep)
items.q: Six tweets T1–T6 have relevance scores 3, 2, 0, 1, 3, 2. A ranking algorithm orders them T4, T1, T6, T3, T5, T2 (relevances 1, 3, 2, 0, 3, 2). Using DCG@k = Σ (2^relᵢ − 1) / log₂(i + 1) and NDCG@k = DCG@k / IDCG@k, what is the approximate NDCG@6?
items.mark: No options were printed. The TA's worked answer on the next slide gives DCG@6 ≈ 11.852, IDCG@6 ≈ 13.735 and NDCG@6 ≈ 0.86.
items.why: The worked answer has arithmetic slips: the 5th term should be 7 / log₂6 ≈ 2.708, not 3.866, and the ideal ranking (3, 3, 2, 2, 1, 0) gives IDCG@6 ≈ 14.595. Recomputed with the stated formula, DCG@6 ≈ 10.693 and NDCG@6 ≈ 0.733.
